metadataFromPriorUpload.title: Where Genetic Variation Comes From: Meiosis, Fertilisation and Mutation | Year 12 Biology Module 6
metadataFromPriorUpload.description:
Full lesson, notes and practice questions: https://hscscience.com.au/subjects/biology/year12/module6/lesson06

In 1977 a drought on Daphne Major killed most of the island's medium ground finches, and the survivors' chicks had deeper beaks, with no new mutation needed. So where does each generation's variation come from? Follow one new allele from the mutation that makes it, through meiosis and fertilisation, see how much each process adds in one generation and over a long time, and why bacteria are different. Two exam-style questions with brief feedback.

0:00 Opening question
0:34 Three sources of variation
1:02 How alleles enter gametes
1:32 New combinations in meiosis
2:01 Fertilisation
2:34 Variation in one generation
3:17 Where new alleles originate
3:53 Variation in bacteria
4:28 Memory
4:51 Practice question 1
5:33 Answer 1
6:04 Practice question 2
6:29 Answer 2
6:56 Decision rule
7:25 Key notes

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 6, Genetic Change. Inquiry question: "How does mutation introduce new alleles into a population?"
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 6):
"investigate the causes of genetic variation relating to the processes of fertilisation, meiosis and mutation (ACSBL078)"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Mutation practice: HSC-style questions. Next: How mutation, gene flow and drift change a gene pool.
